description: Use small shells around a forced K4 or independent 4-set as decomposition units. The goal is to expose stronger local rigidity before the SAT back end sees the branch.
mathematical_formalization: Define shell S around a constrained 4-vertex pattern and branch on boundary types B(S), measuring whether B(S) collapses unknown-edge structure faster than split-vertex gluing.
implementation_hypothesis: Construct shell signatures from local forbidden-pattern templates and benchmark them on the same proof ladder as H2 pair splits.
experiment_seed: Measure unknown-edge count and proof-core reuse under K4-shell vs independent-4-shell partitions.

closest_prior_art.title: Decreasing the upper bound on the Ramsey number R(5,5)

novelty_claim: A shell primitive could compress the residue at the representation level before any solver optimization.
differentiation: The claim fails immediately if the shell representation does not outperform the current split/gluing language.
